Electric.text: • In March 2025, WPL filed a retail electric and gas rate review with the PSCW for the 2026/2027 forward-looking Test Period. The key drivers for the filing include revenue requirement impacts of increasing electric and gas rate base, including wind refurbishment projects, energy storage, existing natural gas-fired EGU improvements, solar generation costs incurred that exceed the construction cost estimates previously approved by the PSCW, and electric and gas distribution investments. The filing requested approval for WPL to implement increases in annual rates for its retail electric and gas customers of $120 million and $9 million in 2026, respectively, with any granted rate changes expected to be effective on January 1, 2026. WPL’s filing also requested approval to implement an additional increase in annual rates for its retail electric and gas customers of $82 million and $5 million in 2027, respectively, with any granted rate changes expected to be effective on January 1, 2027. WPL also requested a return on common equity of 9.9% and to implement a common equity component of its regulatory capital structure of 55.5% in 2026 and 55.3% in 2027.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: There was no single customer whose revenues were 10% or more of Alliant Energy’s, IPL’s and WPL’s respective consolidated revenues.
First 50 basis points | 75% customers, 25% IPL
>50 to 100 basis points | 50% customers, 50% IPL
>100 to 150 basis points | 25% customers, 75% IPL
>150 basis points | 100% customers

Electric Supply - Alliant Energy, IPL and WPL have met, and expect to continue meeting, customer demand for electricity through a mix of electric supply, including owned EGUs, PPAs and additional purchases from wholesale energy markets.

IPL and WPL utilize accredited capacity from EGUs they own, and have rights to through PPAs, to meet a substantial portion of their current MISO planning reserve margin requirements and periodically rely on short-term market capacity purchases to supplement the accredited capacity from such EGUs.
Our ability to timely obtain rate adjustments to earn authorized rates of return depends upon timely regulatory action under applicable statutes and regulations, and cannot be guaranteed.
We rely on third parties for software to protect against cyber attacks and we are at risk if such third parties are targets of cyber attacks.

Supply chain disruptions could negatively impact our operations and implementation of our strategy - Our operations and strategy depend on the global supply chain to procure the equipment, materials and other resources necessary to provide services in a safe and reliable manner and construct new utility infrastructure.
We face risks related to non-utility operations - We rely on our non-utility operations for a portion of our earnings.
The primary sources of funds for Alliant Energy to pay dividends to its shareowners are dividends and distributions from its subsidiaries, primarily its utility subsidiaries.

The ability of our subsidiaries to pay dividends or make distributions to Alliant Energy and, accordingly, our ability to pay dividends on Alliant Energy common stock will depend on regulatory limitations, earnings, cash flows, capital requirements and general financial condition of our subsidiaries.
Any potential liability depends on a number of factors outside of our control.
We rely on our strong credit ratings to access the credit markets.
The ability to achieve these goals will depend on future economic developments, evolving energy technologies and emerging trends in Alliant Energy’s service territories.
Primary Sources and Uses of Cash - Alliant Energy’s most significant source of cash is from electric and gas sales to IPL’s and WPL’s customers.
